lines.say: This practice exam covers all of Unit 1. Do it under exam conditions.
About 50 minutes for short answers, 25 for the 20 multiple-choice.
30 marks plus 20 marks. That's 50 marks in total.
Mark honestly. Only give a mark when your answer has the listed point.
For a cube, SA to V ratio is 6 divided by the side length.
1 centimetre: six to one. 2 centimetres: three to one. 4 centimetres: one and a half to one.

draw.alt: Cubes of side 1, 2 and 4 cm with SA:V ratios falling

lines.say: Bigger cells have too little membrane for their volume. Exchange is too slow.
Only prokaryotes have DNA in a nucleoid with no membrane. A wall proves nothing.
Potato strips in sucrose. In pure water, mass goes up 18 percent.
Water moved in by osmosis, towards the higher solute concentration.
Find where the change crosses zero. Between 0.2 and 0.4, about 0.3 molar.

draw.alt: Graph of percentage mass change against sucrose concentration crossing zero near 0.3 M

lines.say: In 0.6 molar, the cells are plasmolysed. The membrane pulls from the wall.
S phase: the DNA is replicated, making sister chromatids.
Mitosis of a 46-chromosome cell gives two identical cells, each with 46.
Broken tumour suppressor genes let damaged cells keep dividing.
Higher humidity means a smaller gradient, so transpiration and uptake fall.

draw.alt: Water vapour leaving a stoma; as humidity rises, the outward arrow shrinks

lines.say: Water rises by tension, cohesion and adhesion. No ATP needed.
Blood glucose rises. Beta cells detect it and release insulin.
Cells take up glucose, the liver stores glycogen, and glucose falls. Negative feedback.
In type 1 diabetes, the immune system destroyed the beta cells. No insulin.
Eating less sugar isn't enough. Insulin itself must be replaced.
Temperature is the independent variable. Bubbles of CO two are the dependent.
Control the yeast amount, sugar concentration and volume, and timing.
One trial per temperature isn't reliable. Do replicates and take a mean.
Or use a gas syringe, because bubbles vary in size.
Try every question before you look at a solution.
Answer the command word, and use the marks as a guide.
Go back to the lesson for any topic where you dropped marks.
